bind.label: Bind Address
bind.help: IP address to bind the server to (0.0.0.0 for all interfaces)

port.label: Port
port.help: Port on which the web server will listen

auth.label: Enable Authentication
auth.help: Enable ioBroker user authentication for the web server

_oauthIntro.text: MCP clients such as Claude Desktop connect through a browser login instead of a token you create by hand. The client never sees the ioBroker password and discovers the server on its own.

_oauthNeedsAuth.text: Enable 'Authentication' first — without it the MCP endpoint is open and OAuth has nothing to protect.

_oauthExtensionHint.text: As a web extension the selected web instance provides the login: OAuth must be enabled there as well ('Allow third-party clients'), otherwise MCP clients only get a redirect to the login page, which they cannot use.

_oauthHttpsWarning.text: OAuth without HTTPS: remote MCP clients refuse plain http:// and will not be able to connect. Enable SSL, or put this server behind an https reverse proxy and set the public URL.

publicUrl.label: Public URL
publicUrl.help: Externally reachable address of this server, without a path. Required behind a reverse proxy. As a web extension it must match the public URL of the web instance.
publicUrl.validatorErrorText: Enter an address like https://iobroker.example.com - scheme and host only, no path

oauthDynamicRegistration.label: Allow client self-registration
oauthDynamicRegistration.help: MCP clients register themselves automatically. With this off, every client has to be registered by hand before it can connect.

allowSetState.label: Allow setting states
allowSetState.help: Allow MCP clients to write state values and to acknowledge system notifications (set_state, set_states, clear_notifications tools)

setStateDestructive.label: Mark setting states as destructive
setStateDestructive.help: Declare set_state/set_states as destructive (destructiveHint), so MCP clients can warn before writing. Whether a client still asks for confirmation when this is off depends on the client.

allowObjectChange.label: Allow object/file changes
allowObjectChange.help: Allow MCP clients to create/modify objects, aliases and scenes and to write files (set_object, create_alias, write_file tools). Off by default.

allowInstanceControl.label: Allow controlling instances
allowInstanceControl.help: Start, stop and restart adapter instances and change their log level (start_instance, stop_instance, restart_instance, set_log_level tools). Off by default.

allowAdapterManagement.label: Allow managing adapters
allowAdapterManagement.help: Add and delete instances and upgrade adapters from the repository (add_instance, delete_instance, upgrade_adapter tools). Off by default.

allowScriptChange.label: Allow changing scripts
allowScriptChange.help: Create, change, start/stop and delete scripts of the javascript adapter and run code once (set_script, enable_script, delete_script, run_script tools). Reading scripts is always allowed. Off by default.

_allowScriptChangeWarning.text: Scripts run with full access to ioBroker. Only enable this for MCP clients you trust.

sendToAllowlist.label: Allow messages to adapters
sendToAllowlist.help: Adapters or instances the send_to tool may send messages to, separated by commas; * allows all. Empty: no send_to tool.

confirmDangerous.label: Ask for confirmation before dangerous actions
confirmDangerous.help: MCP clients that support it (elicitation) ask the user before an object or instance is deleted, an instance stopped, an adapter upgraded or installed, a script saved or run, or a message sent. Other clients rely on their own confirmation.

allowPackageInstall.label: Allow installing packages (developers only)
allowPackageInstall.help: Only relevant for adapter developers: MCP clients may install adapter packages (npm, GitHub, URL or .tgz file) on an ioBroker host (install_package tool). Off by default.

_allowPackageInstallWarning.text: This option is meant for developing adapters on a test system, e.g. to let an AI agent install a freshly packed .tgz. An installed package runs with full rights on the host. Never enable it on a productive system or for clients you do not fully trust.

certPublic.label: Public Certificate
certPublic.help: Path to the public certificate file

certPrivate.label: Private Key
certPrivate.help: Path to the private key file

certChained.label: Chained Certificate
certChained.help: Path to the chained certificate file (optional)
